service.description:
The time entries the user may see, narrowed, sorted and paged, for TimeEntries and ProjectTime (design-projects.md §8; no entity filter covers TimeEntry, impl-projects.md F1). A person's time is seen by the person, the managers of the projects it is on (ProjectManager or Manager: the entries on the project and its items), the person's line managers (PrtManager), and everyone's by ADMIN and, when the user's timesheet policy has approvers any, by the holders of TIMESHEET_APPROVE.
The find: partyId, rootWorkEffortId (the project's entries and its items'), workEffortId (one item), noWorkItem, clientPartyId, workTypeEnumId, billable (Y or N), clientInvoiced and workerInvoiced (Y or N), sheetStatus (open: In-Process or none, returned, submitted, approved, locked: submitted or approved), fromDate and thruDate (an entry whose fromDate is in the period), text (in the comments), timeEntryIds. orderByField one of fromDate, hours, partyId, workEffortId (with - for descending; default -fromDate).
A row: {timeEntryId, partyId, personName, workEffortId, workEffortName, workEffortTypeEnumId, rootWorkEffortId, projectName, fromDate and thruDate (millis), running, hours, breakHours, workTypeEnumId, workTypeLabel, rateTypeEnumId, billable, comments, clientPartyId, timesheetId, sheetStatusId (In-Process when none), returned, locked (its week submitted or approved under a locking policy), invoiceId, vendorInvoiceId, invoiced}; with rates (withRates, for ADMIN and holders of TIME_ENTRY_RATE: those who manage money) also clientHourRate, vendorHourRate, clientAmount and vendorAmount (hours times the rate: the entry's own hour rate, else its RateAmount's, impl-projects.md F86). totals (withTotals, over every match, not the page): hours, billableHours, nonBillableHours, entryCount, byPerson, byWorkType and byItem (hours of each, with an item's estimate), and with rates clientAmount and vendorAmount.

The time import (design-projects.md §8 ImportTime, §15 Time import): the Time entries CSV, a header line then a row per entry with date (yyyy-MM-dd), person (email or user name; a full name with one match; empty: partyId), work item key or project key (an item column, else a project column), hours (decimal or h:mm[:ss]) or start and end times (HH:mm, or a date and time), work type (its id or name), billable (yes or no; empty yes) and comment. The headers are matched by their words, so the detailed exports of Toggl, Harvest and Clockify read with at most a column renamed (their own presets come later, §16); the delimiter is the header line's commonest of comma, semicolon and tab.
Each row is planned: the person, the item (a task or project the user sees), the work type, billable, the time (hours rounded to the person's policy's smallest entry, a warning when that changed; rows with hours only stack from 9:00 on their person's day), and what it will do: create, skip (an entry of the person on the item starting at the same moment is there already) or fail with its problems (no date, no person found, a work item not found or not visible, no hours, a work item required by the policy, a future day the policy refuses, a week the user may not change, or one submitted and locked). preview true plans only (previewList, the first maxRows); otherwise each row to create goes through store#TimeEntry in its own transaction: a row that fails is logged and named with its reason, the others are imported. progressUserId gets the progress on the topic timeImportProgress every 25 rows and at the end. The file comes as an upload (timeEntryFile), text (fileText) or a resource location (fileLocation).
